routes.speaker: James White
routes.position: The canonical Gospel accounts of Jesus are authentic and historically accurate

bridges.burden: Show that the canonical Gospel narratives can be trusted as authentic reports of events in Jesus's life.

Show that apparent differences can coexist as complementary testimony rather than incompatible invention.
Defend the possibility and purposive selectivity of divine action in history.

Connect resurrection and prophetic fulfillment to the historically grounded apostolic proclamation.

routes.speaker: John Dominic Crossan
routes.position: The Gospels are developing theological interpretations rather than one uniformly historical account

bridges.burden: Deny that there is one uniformly historical orthodox account by showing multiple developing versions.
Show that literary dependence reduces the force of treating the Gospels as independent witnesses.
Explain Gospel differences as Spirit-guided contextual adaptation for different communities.
Argue that Gospel narratives may convey authentic theological truth without being literal history.
Defend reading divine presence consistently with nature rather than as selective supernatural intervention.
Interpret Christological titles and stories against Roman imperial claims and programs.
Explain prophecy language as retrospective interpretation of Jesus through Israel's hopes and righteous sufferers.
